newsitem.title: HUNGARY: DG Bank plans to invest in Hungary unit.
newsitem.headline: DG Bank plans to invest in Hungary unit.

text.p: Germany's DG Bank plans to invest at least 1.4 billion forints and 20 million marks in the Hungarian savings cooperatives sector in the next few years, DG Bank said on Thursday.

DG Bank recently won a privatisation tender for 55.98 percent of Takarekbank, umbrella bank of Hungary's savings cooperatives, while Hungaria Biztosito, the insurance unit of Germany's Allianz will buy a five percent stake.
The shares in Takarekbanl will be sold by the state privatisation agency APV at some 531 percent of the face value, the highest price ever in Hungarian bank privatisations.

Friedbert Malt, member of DG Bank's board if directors told a news conference that Takarekbank should concentrate on cooperation with large and international companies, including DG's German clients, and strengthen its umbrella bank role.
DG also planned to help the introduction of modern deposit products in Hungarian savings cooperatives.
"The investments needed to carry out these plans total some 20 million German marks," DG said in a statement.
Malt added that DG also undertook to increase Takarekbank's capital by some 700 forints to two billion forints.

DG will subscribe the shares to be issued in the capital increase at 200 percent of the face value, and 700 million forints of the funds from the capital rise will boost Takarekbank's reserves, he said.

DG expects the umbrella bank and the 231 savings cooperatives, which have more than 1,600 outlets, to increase their combined market share from five percent to 10 percent in the next few years, Malt said.
However, the banking group has to fight for the retail market with strong competitors, such as OTP Bank and Postabank, he added.
Hungary's savings cooperatives, holding a stake of 33 percent in Takarekbank, have an option to acquire a majority in the umbrella bank in five years, Malt said.
